Update on Letter of Intent

On 10 September 2026, the board of directors of Bidco and Eleco made an announcement pursuant to Rule 2.7 of the Takeover Code (the “Rule 2.7 Announcement”) of a recommended all-cash acquisition by Bidco of the entire issued and to be issued ordinary share capital of Eleco (the “Acquisition”), intended to be implemented by means of a Court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the 2006 Act (the “Scheme”).

The circular in relation to the Scheme was published or made available to Eleco Shareholders on 2 October 2026 (the “Scheme Document”). Unless defined herein, defined terms shall have the meanings given to them in the Scheme Document.

As set out in the Rule 2.7 Announcement, Bidco had received a non-binding letter of intent from Raymond James Wealth Management Limited, trading as Charles Stanley (“Charles Stanley”) dated 8 September 2026 to exercise (or procure the exercise of) voting rights in favour of the resolutions relating to the Scheme and the Acquisition at the Meetings (or in the event that the Acquisition is implemented by an Offer, to accept or procure the acceptance of such Offer) in respect of 6,343,418 Eleco Shares, representing approximately 7.5 per cent. of the existing issued ordinary share capital of Eleco as at the last Business Day before the date of the Rule 2.7 Announcement (the “Charles Stanley Letter of Intent”).

Under the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent, Charles Stanley is permitted to sell, acquire or otherwise deal in Eleco Shares at any time.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 1 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold a total of 765,127 Eleco Shares in the period between the Rule 2.7 Announcement and 29 September 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 5 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold a total of 9,660 Eleco Shares on 30 September 2026 and 42,340 Eleco Shares on 1 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 7 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold 98,280 Eleco Shares on 2 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 8 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold 4,300 and 103,185 Eleco Shares on 5 and 6 October 2026, respectively.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 12 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had transferred out 9,500 Eleco Shares from its discretionary holding on 6 October 2026 and sold 204,860 Eleco Shares on 8 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 13 October 2026, Bidco became aware that of the 24,980 Eleco Shares sold by Charles Stanley on 9 October 2026, 8,670 Eleco Shares were subject to the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 14 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold 3,610 Eleco Shares on 12 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 15 October 2026, Bidco became aware that of the 645,810 Eleco Shares sold by Charles Stanley on 13 October 2026, 640,810 Eleco Shares were subject to the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 19 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold a total of 55,220 Eleco Shares since the previous Form 8.3 announcement released by Charles Stanley on 14 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 22 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold 374,050 Eleco Shares on 20 October 2026.

Pursuant to the Form 8.3 announcement released by Charles Stanley on 22 October 2026, Bidco became aware that of the 238,660 Eleco Shares sold by Charles Stanley on 21 October 2026, 13,660 Eleco Shares were subject to the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent.

Therefore, the total number of Eleco Shares which are subject to the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent has been reduced to 4,010,146 Eleco Shares, representing approximately 4.8 per cent. of the existing issued ordinary share capital of Eleco as at the close of business on the last Business Day prior to this announcement.

data.title: Genmab Says Ovarian Cancer Drug Met Two Endpoints in Phase 3 Trial
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Genmab's ovarian cancer treatment met both its primary endpoint and a key secondary endpoint in a Phase 3 trial.

The company said Friday that Rina-S, or rinatabart sesutecan, significantly reduced the risk of disease progression in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, meeting a primary endpoint of progression-free survival.

The drug also met a key secondary endpoint of significantly improving overall survival among patients in the study.

Shares gained 6.8% on the news to $42.73 as of midday Friday. The stock is up 39% this year.

"These results advance our ambition to become a leader in gynecologic oncology and reflect our commitment to improving the lives of patients with high unmet medical needs," Chief Executive Officer Jan van de Winkel said.

The company said it plans to engage with global regulatory authorities to discuss potential next steps.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: CVS Caremark, Express Scripts, Optum Rx targeted in House investigation
data.description:
Key points:
  • The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform has launched an investigation into whether CVS Caremark , Express Scripts, and Optum Rx engaged in punitive audits against independent pharmacies as punishment for supporting legislation to reform the pharmacy benefit manager industry.
  • "In the short span of time since the Committee’s July markup of H.R. 6610, the Pharmacists Fight Back in FEHB Plans Act, multiple independent pharmacies that supported the Committee’s efforts have received an unusual number of audit notices for minuscule prescription charges after the stated compliance deadline date from CVS Caremark," Chairman James Comer (R-Ky.) writes in his letter to CVS Caremark.
  • One audit conducted by a PBM was over a drug that cost $0.99 "that resulted in hundreds of hours of staff time for the independent pharmacy," according to a news release.
  • Comer is asking for information from the three PBMs related to audits conducted from July 22 to the present.
  • Express Scripts is owned by Cigna , while Optum Rx is a part of UnitedHealth .

data.title: American Express To Cut 5% Of Global Workforce; Raises 2026 EPS Outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • American Express posted adjusted EPS of $4.68, beating expectations of $4.49, while revenue of $20.06 billion came in just below the $20.12 billion estimate, according to Fiscal AI.
  • Provisions for credit losses fell to $1.0 billion from $1.3 billion a year earlier.
  • Net interest income rose 10% year over year to $4.94 billion, supported by growth in cardmember balances.

American Express Company (AXP) shares drew investor attention on Friday after the company reported third-quarter results and raised its full-year 2026 earnings per share (EPS) outlook while maintaining its revenue growth forecast.

On the Q3 earnings call, CEO Stephen Squeri said American Express recorded a $336 million restructuring charge and plans to eliminate approximately 5% of its global workforce as it seeks to improve organizational efficiency and agility.

AXP shares traded 3.5% lower at the time of writing.

Earnings And Guidance

American Express reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $4.68, beating consensus forecast of $4.49, while revenue of $20.06 billion came in below the $20.12 billion estimate, according to estimates compiled by Fiscal AI.

Net income rose 28% year over year to $3.71 billion, while diluted EPS increased 31% to $5.42 from $4.14. Adjusted EPS excludes the gain from the sale of the company’s equity interest in Global Business Travel Group (GBTG), net of the portion used to fund restructuring. The sale generated a $982 million pretax gain, while the restructuring charge was $336 million pretax.

Net interest income(NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 10% year-over-year to $4.94 billion, supported by growth in cardmember balances.

“Our business momentum continues, with strength in billings, new acquisitions and Card Member retention, and excellent credit quality,” CEO Stephen Squeri said.

Spending, Credit And Margins

According to management’s earnings-call commentary, billed business increased 8% to $454 billion, with travel and entertainment spending up 10%, airline spending up 13% and restaurant spending up 9%.

However the company reported consolidated provisions for credit losses of $1.0 billion, down from $1.3 billion a year earlier, reflecting a reserve release compared with a reserve build in the prior-year quarter, partially offset by higher net write-offs.

CFO Christophe Le Caillec said return on equity had risen from an average of 25%–28% about a decade ago to approximately 35% more recently. He also said the company expects variable customer engagement expense growth to moderate significantly in Q4 as it laps the prior-year U.S. Platinum Card refresh.

2026 Outlook

American Express maintained its full-year revenue growth forecast of 10% and raised reported EPS guidance to $18.30–$18.60, equivalent to 19%–21% growth. Adjusted EPS guidance rose to $17.60–$17.90, equivalent to 14%–16% growth.

Separately, Squeri said costs associated with remediation related to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) matter were not anticipated to affect 2027 guidance.

How Retail Views AXP 

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ a day ago, amid ‘high’ message volumes. AXP was also among the platform’s trending tickers at the time of writing.

AXP shares have dropped over 17% year-to-date.

data.title: AT&T, T-Mobile tighten AI guardrails as autonomous networks remain years away
data.description:
By Mehnaz Yasmin and Harshita Mary Varghese

Telecom giants AT&T and T-Mobile are investing to safeguard customer data and network infrastructure from new cybersecurity threats as AI integration ramps up, though fully autonomous networks remain years away, company executives told Reuters.

As AI agents automate workflows and data analysis, with declining human intervention, cybersecurity concerns are growing across industries over access to sensitive information and connected software.

For telecom operators, which manage vast amounts of customer data and critical communications infrastructure, vulnerabilities in AI systems or third-party software could extend from data breaches to network disruptions.

"Yes, we are increasing our investments in how we monitor and react," T-Mobile's Chief Technology Officer John Saw told the Reuters Global Markets Forum. The company simultaneously works with vendors to ensure security holes are closed as soon as possible, he added.

The Bellevue, Washington-based wireless carrier has suffered several data breaches, including incidents in 2021 and 2023, cumulatively impacting over 100 million customer accounts. It has agreed to various settlements with consumers and the Federal Communications Commission involving cybersecurity penalties and investments.

AT&T, meanwhile, warned that third-party software providers and AI agents pose cybersecurity risks that extend beyond operators' own networks.

"There (are) industry problems, not things that AT&T can solve by itself," CTO Jeremy Legg said, questioning if the open-source community followed comparable security standards.

The Texas-based company has deployed AI governance controls such as encryption, multi-factor authentication and human oversight of data access. It is also working to verify whether third-party AI agents seeking access to customer accounts are acting on behalf of legitimate customers, the company said.

AI has automated aspects of network management for telecom operators, but handing over entire networks to AI-driven autonomous systems is still "years away," Legg said, as human intervention is still required to solve complex network problems.

For instance, AT&T has automated some tasks such as analyzing trouble tickets to identify potential fixes and, in some cases, automatically implementing repairs. T-Mobile, meanwhile, uses AI to automatically adjust cell-site antennas when nearby sites go down to compensate for coverage gaps.

During Winter Storm Fern in January, T-Mobile's self-organizing network, or SON, restored coverage to about 66% of customers within an hour and 90% within eight hours, with most customers regaining service before power was restored, Saw said.

data.title: CPC Blend diffs ease after deal
data.description:
CPC Blend differentials weakened after a deal in the trading window as high freight and demurrage rates, unstable supply and high security risks for ships in the Black Sea weigh on the prices, traders said.

They said extremely high freight rates have effectively shut down arbitrage shipments of CPC Blend outside the region.

PLATTS WINDOW

  • There were no bids or offers on Friday for CPC Blend, Urals and Azeri BTC, traders said.

  • On Thursday, Vitol sold to BP a Suezmax cargo of CPC Blend for loading on Nov. 11-15 at dated Brent minus $7.00 per barrel, well below recent estimates.

NEWS

  • The first Russian diesel bound for the US following a surprise agreement reached between Moscow and US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed on Friday.

  • Russian oil sellers have raised ESPO Blend offers to China to record levels, supported by strong demand and higher freight costs driven by the Iran war, although some independent Chinese refiners may baulk as margins turn negative.

data.title: Piper Sandler maintains Overweight rating on Estee Lauder Cos, $125 price target
data.description:
Piper Sandler maintained their Overweight rating on Estee Lauder Cos's stock with a price target of $125.00.

The price target implies an upside of 16.0% from the Oct 22 close of $107.72.

Key takeaways from the analyst note

Strong Innovation Pipeline: Estée Lauder has significantly improved its innovation pipeline, particularly in skincare, with 14 major product launches in F1Q27 compared to 9 in the prior year. This increase in new product introductions is expected to enhance sales growth, particularly as innovation is projected to rise as a percentage of total sales.

Resilient Market Demand: The rebound in China's passenger traffic and overall beauty sales indicates a favorable environment for Estée Lauder's products, especially in travel retail, which constitutes 15% of its sales. This recovery supports the company's growth outlook and aligns with management's expectations for continued momentum in the prestige beauty market.
